excavations.research_focus: Palace architecture, sculptures, orthostats, and urban organization
excavations.description: Excavations at Tell Halaf documented the monumental center associated with Guzana and Bit-Bahiani. The palace and sculptural remains are central evidence for northern Mesopotamian political art and architecture.

excavations.research_focus: Citadel, gates, palaces, sculptures, inscriptions, and city planning
excavations.description: Excavations at Zincirli revealed a fortified urban center with monumental gates, royal buildings, sculptures, and inscriptions. The evidence makes Sam’al one of the most important sites for studying political and cultural interaction in the northern Levant.

excavations.period_studied: Bronze Age through Iron Age and later occupation
excavations.research_focus: Settlement sequence, urban development, inscriptions, and regional exchange
excavations.description: Excavation of the Hama mound established a long occupational sequence and provided evidence for the urban history of the Orontes valley. Iron Age inscriptions and architecture are read within a setting that included Luwian, Aramaic, and other regional traditions.

excavations.research_focus: Urban settlement, regional political networks, and the Lu’ash context
excavations.description: Fieldwork at Tell Afis contributes to the study of Iron Age settlement and political organization in northern Syria. The site is considered in relation to Hazrek, Lu’ash, Hamath, and the wider network documented by inscriptions such as the Zakkur Stele.

excavations.research_focus: Palace and temple architecture, administration, and Neo-Hittite-Aramean interaction
excavations.description: Excavations at Tell Tayinat have documented monumental buildings and administrative contexts associated with Kunulua. The remains are important for studying the mixed political and cultural traditions of the Amuq plain.

excavations.research_focus: Palace architecture, wall paintings, inscriptions, and changing administration
excavations.description: Excavation at Tell Ahmar documented the urban center of Til Barsip and its later Assyrian-period occupation. The site is valuable for tracing political change on the Euphrates and the transformation of local institutions under imperial rule.

excavations.research_focus: City gate, fortifications, cultic installations, and settlement organization
excavations.description: Excavation at et-Tell exposed fortifications, a monumental gate, and cultic contexts associated by some researchers with Bethsaida and Geshur. The interpretation remains tied to the specific archaeological and historical evidence rather than to an automatic ethnic identification.

excavations.research_focus: Gate complex, cultic area, settlement layers, and the Tel Dan Stele
excavations.description: Excavations at Tel Dan documented successive settlement layers, monumental architecture, and the Tel Dan Stele. Together these remains illuminate regional political history and the use of Aramaic in the southern Levant.

excavations.research_focus: Fortifications, temples, churches, houses, documents, and funerary contexts
excavations.description: Excavations at Dura-Europos revealed a multilingual frontier city with civic, military, domestic, religious, and funerary buildings. The site provides a broad comparative context for Aramaic use across different communities and administrations.
